Load the libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
options(scipen = 999)

Data

For this homework, we are going to use the Gapminder data on population (pop), GDP per capita (gdp), and life expectancy (lex). These data were downloaded and compiled using the gapminder_compile.Rmd script in the data folder.

Let’s focus our attention on data from the past 100 years, between 1925 and 2025.

gapminder <- read_csv("data/gapminder.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(between(year, 1925, 2025))
  1. Use the function(s) of your choice to get an idea of the overall structure of the data, including its dimensions, column names, classes, etc.
glimpse(gapminder)

## Columns: 5

  1. How many countries are represented in this dataset?
gapminder %>% 
  summarize(n_distinct(country))

  1. Which five countries have had the largest absolute population growth between 1925-2025? Show this as a table.
pop_growth <- gapminder %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1925, 2025)) %>%
  select(country, year, pop) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year,
              values_from = pop) %>%
  mutate(Pop_growth = `2025` - `1925`) %>%
  arrange(desc(Pop_growth)) %>%
  head(5)

pop_growth

  1. Make a plot that shows population growth over time for the top country you found in question #3.
 gapminder %>% 
  filter(country == "India") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=year, y=pop))+
  geom_line(color = "steelblue")+
  geom_point(shape=5)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1925,2025,by=10),minor_breaks = NULL)+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1))+
  labs(title="Population Growth from 1925 to 2025 in India", x="year", y="population")

  1. Has global life expectancy changed between 1925 and 2025? Show the min, median, mean, and max for all countries (combined) in the dataset.
gapminder %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1925, 2025)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>% 
  summarise(
    min_life= min(lex, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_life = median(lex, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_life= mean(lex, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_life = max(lex, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
## # A tibble: 2 × 5
##    year min_life median_life mean_life max_life
##   <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
## 1  1925     21.0        35.9      38.1     63.5
## 2  2025     52.8        74.8      73.9     85.6

Answer: Yes

  1. Make a plot that shows the distribution of life expectancy for all countries in 1925 and 2025 (try using geom_density). What do you notice about the shift in life expectancy over time?
gapminder %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1925, 2025)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lex, group = factor(year), fill = factor(year))) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Life Expectancy Distribution (1925 vs 2025)",
    x = "Life Expectancy",
    fill = "Year"
  ) 
## Warning: Removed 13 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_density()`).

# Answer: Compared to 1925, the life expectancy in 2025 demonstrates a great increase. 7. We are interested in the relationship between per capita GDP and life expectancy; i.e. does having more money help you live longer in 2025? Show this as a plot. (Suggestion! Remove Monaco as an extreme outlier.)

gapminder %>%
  filter(year == 2025, country != "Monaco") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = gdp, y = lex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "GDP per Capita vs Life Expectancy in 2025",
    x = "GDP per Capita (log scale)",
    y = "Life Expectancy"
  ) 
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_smooth()`).
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

  1. Which five countries have had the highest absolute GDP per capita growth over the past 50 years? Show this as a table. (Suggestion! Remove Monaco as an extreme outlier.)
gapminder %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1975, 2025), country != "Monaco") %>%
  select(country, year, gdp) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = gdp) %>%
  mutate(GDP_growth = `2025` - `1975`) %>%
  arrange(desc(GDP_growth)) %>%
  head(5) %>% 
  pull(country)
## [1] "Singapore"  "Ireland"    "Luxembourg" "Guyana"     "Norway"
  1. How does per capita GDP growth compare between these same five countries over the past 50 years? Show this as a plot.
gapminder %>%
  filter(year >= 1975, country == "Singapore"| country == "Ireland"|country == "Luxembourg"|country == "Guyana"|country== "Norway" ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = gdp, color = country)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "GDP per Capita Growth in Top 5 Countries from 1975–2025",
    x = "Year",
    y = "GDP per Capita (log 10)",
    color = "Country"
  )

  1. Do one analysis of your choice that includes a table and plot as outputs.
#What are the top 3 countries with the biggest life expectancy increase from 1975 to 2025. How do the trends increase visually? Use a plot to demonstrate
gapminder %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1975, 2025)) %>%
  select(country, year, lex) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = lex) %>%
  mutate(lex_change = `2025` - `1975`) %>%
  arrange(desc(lex_change)) %>%
  head(3)
## # A tibble: 3 × 4
##   country  `1975` `2025` lex_change
##   <chr>     <dbl>  <dbl>      <dbl>
## 1 Cambodia   24.7   71.0       46.4
## 2 Maldives   51.7   80.5       28.8
## 3 Ethiopia   43.2   70.7       27.5
gapminder %>%
  filter(year >= 1975, country == "Cambodia"| country == "Maldives"|country == "Ethiopia" ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = gdp, color = country)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 3 countries with the biggest life expectancy increase from 1975 to 2025",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Life expectancy",
    color = "Country"
  )
